speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are experiencing occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings following your tympanoplasty. Can you describe when these symptoms began and if you have noticed any discharge or hearing changes since the surgery?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any history of temporomandibular joint dysfunction or jaw clicking, and does pressing on the area in front of your ear reproduce the pain? I would also like to examine your ear canal and jaw joint to rule out mechanical irritation.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the pain is triggered by eating and you have a history of chronic infections, I need to rule out referred pain from the jaw. Do you experience any clicking, popping, or locking in your jaw, and is there tenderness when I press on the muscles just in front of your ear?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: History of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. Underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks prior. Social history: Works as a cashier at a local department store.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the pain radiate from the jaw joint into the ear, and do you notice any grinding of your teeth or clenching of your jaw, especially during stressful moments or while sleeping? I suspect temporomandibular joint disorder is contributing to your symptoms given the trigger of eating and your stress levels.

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal TMJ and otoscopy findings, I suspect a neuroma or nerve irritation from the surgery. Does the pain feel electric or burning, and is the skin over the tragus hypersensitive to light touch?

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal imaging and exam findings, I suspect trigeminal neuralgia or post-surgical nerve irritation. Please confirm if the pain is strictly triggered by chewing or light touch, and if it feels like a sharp electric shock.
